evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep never said the recognizable framing 'Great, it looks like we have availability within your time frame... This will take about 10 to 15 minutes, and you can walk away with a quote you can depend on...' He jumped straight into availability/flexibility discussion without the time-boxed promise and without waiting for an affirmative yes.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Rep asked about the day (Saturday vs. Sunday → Monday), packing level, and heavy items, but never explicitly asked the customer's name, confirmed moving city-to-city route, or approximate home size upfront. Learned it was a one-bedroom only later from his own statement ('typically for a one bedroom').
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move, and what do you want answers to on this call?' The rep moved straight into problem-solving about availability and the safe/furniture issue that the customer raised unprompted.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer volunteered concerns (safe weight, heavy furniture, last-minute timing from mortgage company coordination failure). Rep acknowledged but did not probe deeper with 'tell me more about that' — he pivoted to solutions (suggesting Muscle Movers, discussing equipment and weight limits). N/A credit not applicable because concerns *were* raised; rep simply did not follow the two-layer protocol.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No reflection summary like 'So what I'm hearing is...' The rep listened but never confirmed back a summary of the customer's stated concerns. N/A credit not applicable because the customer did raise concerns.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep gathered: property type (one-bedroom apartment), special items (safe, hardwood furniture, couch, cat tower, guns/ammo). Did NOT systematically ask about floors/stories, number of rooms, walking distance, additional stops, or general room count beyond 'one bedroom.' Collected details reactively through the safe/furniture discussion and special-items checklist at the end, not proactively.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Yes — 'And you were needing full packing into boxes as well' and 'we would typically for a one bedroom we do complete the packing and the moving in a day.'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: No — rep never asked 'A typical box count for a home your size is ________, do you have anything like china or a book collection that might put you over a typical count?'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full — rep gave typical range ('typically a one bedroom apartment for the packing usually takes about two and a half to three and a half hours and then moving typically takes around the same amount of time... five to seven hour range') and personalized to this customer's move (safe, heavy furniture, 3-man crew option, packing + moving estimate $1,608, then adjusted option with 3-man crew at $288/hour for roughly $1,616-$1,700 range).
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full — rep disclosed trip fee ($75), hourly rate ($192 weekdays, $288 with 3-man crew), 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments, packing supplies ($189), and framed it as 'we allocate up to $2,000 per move' and 'you just pay for the time that's actually used.' Included insurance, no taxes or credit card fees.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked — rep never said 'Does that feel fair?' or equivalent, and never paused for the customer to respond unprompted. Customer volunteered 'Yeah, that's pretty much what I figured. I was going to be around the 1500 to two grand mark' (positive reaction) but rep did not explicitly ask for that reaction or hold silence.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full — 'And then we do have an on time guarantee if we're ever late we give you money back.'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full — 'And then also in our hourly rate is our no worries damage coverage. So we pat and wrap everything but we also allocate up to $2,000 per move to give you a peace of mind that any damages that would occur. We cover it way above and beyond the industry standard of 60¢ per pound.'
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False — rep did not ask a version of 'Does that put those to rest?' after delivering the two promises. He moved directly to confirming the safe weight, checking for other items, and scheduling.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked — rep said 'any other questions or anything while we're on the phone here' (throwaway phrasing, automatic no) rather than 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: False — rep did not ask 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' He gathered special items reactively ('you said it was a sleeper couch, right?' / 'And then is there a garage or anything or like a storage') but never asked a catch-all probing question.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Full — 'No, let's go ahead and book it' (customer says this, so rep obtained the yes without softening it into an out). Rep said 'up to you' earlier ('we could always pull it off but up to you') but the ask itself ('we could do Monday with the three man crew...') was plain and led to a clear yes.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: False — rep never mentioned 'rate lock' or that the quoted price is guaranteed/locked in if booked now.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial — confirmed arrival time window (8:30–9:00 AM Monday), crew size (3-man), apartment number (5206), and special considerations (safe, heavy furniture, cat tower, couch, bench). Did NOT explicitly confirm: customer's full address for delivery destination (only the pickup apartment number), customer's phone number (for morning-of crew call), or crew-notesheet details beyond mentioning they'd be in the confirmation email. Email confirmation promised but not read aloud.

top_strength: Calvin handled a high-pressure, last-minute logistics problem with poise: the customer needed help on an impossible timeline with a heavy safe and furniture, and Calvin offered transparent pricing, equipment solutions (dolly types, 3-man crew upgrade), and clear next steps without panic or false promises.
coaching_note: Start every call with the scripted quid pro quo (time-boxed ask + promise of dependable quote) and wait for a yes before probing; also ask their agenda upfront ('Other than price, what are your biggest concerns?') to surface and validate what matters most to them, rather than jumping into problem-solving mode on the first issue they mention.
